utterances.text: It is so admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be given Exhibit D423. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: General, would you now take a look at document -- it's is 65 ter Defence document in your binder. It should be tab 8. Tab 8?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And may we have called up in e-court 00013D.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: General, do you see this document?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: What is being regulated by this document, General?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJOVIC
utterances.text: It says in the heading that pursuant to Amendment 3 of the constitution of the Serbian republic, and then "Official Gazette" of the Serbian people in Bosnia and Herzegovina, number 692 and Article 1 of the law on amendments to the constitutional law on the implementation of the constitution of the Serbian Republic, "Official Gazette" of the Serbian people of Bosnia and Herzegovina, number 6-92, the Presidency of the Serbian republic issues the following decree on appointing judges, jurors, military prosecutors, and deputy military prosecutors. And then under number 1, the following persons are appointed to the supreme military court in Sarajevo: Vidoje Ijacic, judge to the military court in Sarajevo; Damjan Kaurinovic, judge; Delimir [phoen] Jakic, judge to the military court in Bijeljina; Ljubomir Kitic, judge to the military court in Bileca, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: General, I'll interrupt you there, we don't need to have all the names read out. I'm just going to ask you the following question: From this document we see that to the Supreme Military Court in Sarajevo just one person is being appointed, just one person; right?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJOVIC
utterances.text: That is right. But this is probably an amendment. Perhaps the court has other judges as well, but this judge is being additionally appointed so that the court should have the full number of members and then we have the judge-jurors, and military prosecutors and deputies, so judges are appointed by decree of the Presidency of the Serbian republic which is how it should be legally and adapted to the system on the SFRY on the appointment of judges and prosecutors. Now, all these of the [indiscernible] that succeed and then set up their own legal system and judiciary, they based their new laws on the previous laws of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia which is quite in order because everything was in order in that system for that particular system to function.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to tender this document in evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D424. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Yes, Mr. Zorko.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: Now, General, take a look at the next document in your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And may we have it called up in e-court. It is document 00014D.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: General, can you briefly tell us what this document is, what does it regulate, and I'd like to focus your attention on the statement of reasons given in the document.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJOVIC
utterances.text: Well, in the briefest terms we see that this is a decision taken by the authority in the Ministry of Defence of the Army of Republika Srpska, whereby certain persons are taken into service and they are the individuals that were appointed by decree, the one we saw a moment ago, as judges, judge-jurors, prosecutors and so on. We see that at the bottom it says that military courts were established and the following persons admitted. They were all lawyers, I assume, having passed their bar exam and holding the ranks of reserve officers, which tells us that they adhered to the previous SFRY legal provisions whereby judges of military courts and military prosecutors and their deputies, only people can be appointed who have graduated from the Faculty of Law and have passed their bar exam and have a rank. If you do not have a rank, you cannot be a judge. Here I see that all these persons have reserve officer ranks because when they did their military service they attended the reserve officers school and graduated from that school and therefore were given reserve officer ranks and were now being appointed for judges. Looking at their dates of birth, probably they had all previously been working in some of the regular courts of Bosnia-Herzegovina as judges or prosecutors. And this leads us to conclude that under those conditions too, care was taken that only capable people with the necessary educational background and experience were appointed to these posts.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Would you look at paragraph 1 in the statement of reasons.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Next page, please, for the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: And may we have your comments to the paragraph.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJOVIC
utterances.text: Here in the statement it says decision by the Presidency number such and such of the 31st of May, 1992, so already at that time a decision was taken to establish military courts. So the 31st of May, 1992 is the date there, the military court in Sarajevo ceased functioning sometime in mid-May 1995. I left Sarajevo and went to Belgrade on the 28th of May, 1992, so three days later, the military courts were established of the Army of Republika Srpska. I just made it this digression to show you that they acted very speedily.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think it's time for the break, and before we take a break I'd like to tender this document into evidence and that it be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is admitted. May it please be given a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D425.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Indeed you are right, Mr. Zorko, we'll take a break and come back at half past. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zorko.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Can we call up in e-court 65 ter Defence document 00052D.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: General, the document will be appearing on your screen shortly, and you also have it in your binder. We can see that the document issued by the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps command is here, and I'm interested in the term "extraordinary military court" which is in English just below, or a "special military court" which is specifically referred to in Article 9. Can you tell us what this is about when an extraordinary or special military court is referred to in this order?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJOVIC
utterances.text: I can see in the heading that it says: "In view of the fact that the president of Republika Srpska has declared a state of war in the area of responsibility of Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, I hereby order, among other things, that all units are to set up this court." Well, this is in fact an old term renamed. Probably since a state of war was declared a possibility was provided for extraordinary or special military courts to be set up. It follows from this document that a military officer, senior military officer is vested with setting up such a court within his unit to deal with specific issues. This is something that existed for a very short time after World War II up until the 1950s, and at that time there was the possibility of court marshals to be set up and they would use the summary procedure. This possibility was not used at any time afterwards in the SFRY. We can see here that it says that it's a special military court that a commanding officer will set up on an ad hoc basis for the purposes related to his unit. It can have -- and in fact it can be expedited this procedure. We have this term extraordinary military courts abroad, for instance in the American armed forces where an officer at a certain level may set up an extraordinary military court, and of course such courts will not be composed of professional judges or lawyers but rather members of a particular unit. This is in fact a rather nonsensical institution that was provided for within the military system. I don't see whether it can have a purpose really rather than allowing the commander to take a decision on certain matters on the spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D426. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we call up document 00737D.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: General, I don't know if you can see the document.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJOVIC
utterances.text: Can you give me reference for the binder, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: This should be tab 9.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJOVIC
utterances.text: It is not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJOVIC
utterances.text: It's tab 13.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: Yes, apologies, that's right. General, can we have your brief comments on the text below the word "I hereby order," or specifically below item 1.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that this is the order dated 15 August 1995 of the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska. I hereby order, mobilise two lawyers to each unit of the rank of a regiment brigade, through municipal departments through the Ministry of Defence, and assign them to organs for moral guidance, religious and legal afars. The dead-line is 20 August 1995: "The mobilised lawyers shall carry out professional tasks related to the work of extraordinary military courts and shall conduct all disciplinary procedures instigated by commanders of regiments brigades against responsible persons." So we can see in view of the document we looked at earlier on that the commander of the Main Staff decided after all that lawyers should be recruited to provide professional assistance in the work of extraordinary courts; in other words, to say assist those who will be assigned to such extraordinary military courts and furnish them with expertise, which is in legal terms proper and I think also something to be wished for.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Microphone for you, Mr. Zorko.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: We will no longer dwell on this document, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I tender the document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D427. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: General, please take a look at the document behind tab 14 in your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And in e-court, can we call up 65 ter Defence document 00063D.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: General, have look at the document, please, and give us your comments on the nature of the document, what it stands for.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJOVIC
utterances.text: This is a criminal report, in other words, a document which lies at the basis of the initiation of criminal proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: I will stop you there --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Thomas is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I am sorry, Your Honour, I didn't have anything on my screen, but I see that it's just coming.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is precisely what I wanted to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: General, please wait for the document to appear on the screen so that everyone can follow. We have the document on our screens now, General.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJOVIC
utterances.text: The criminal report was submitted to the military prosecutor's office in Bijeljina, which is in Republika Srpska, against Vaso Vujicic, lieutenant of military post 7572 Sarajevo, or rather, Han Pijesak. What is interesting in the professional sense is that Colonel Velibor Jeremic invokes Article 148 para 1 of the criminal procedure law, and this is properly invoked because this is the Law on Criminal Procedure that was taken over from the former Yugoslavia and it is precisely the relevant article. What is also interesting is that he invokes Article 217 of the Criminal Code of Republika Srpska which was normally a piece of legislation which was subordinate to that of the SFRY. It was now renamed Criminal Code of Republika Srpska. And this is something that the prosecutor's office in Bijeljina can invoke for these criminal offences. And it does cover all the requirements and vests the prosecutor with powers to initiate criminal proceedings. That's all that I can say that might be interesting in relation to the criminal report here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I tender the document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D428. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zorko.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: General, look at the next document in your binder, which should be behind tab 14.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And can we call up P822.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: Can you see the document, General?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: General, what sort of proceedings does this involve, procedurally speaking?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJOVIC
utterances.text: This is a lawsuit initiated before the second municipal court in Belgrade for indemnities, plaintiff Dragomir Milosevic, and the second municipal court in Belgrade rendered a decision settling the matter, and this is a lawsuit for indemnities of and -- of non-material damages.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: When we are talking about lawsuits, when a prosecutor is heard, in what capacity would he be heard then? Is there a role for him to play?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJOVIC
utterances.text: In lawsuits, there is a peculiar situation where the plaintiff may in the evidentiary procedure be heard as a party to the lawsuit, so the difference between him being heard in this capacity and the capacity of being heard as a witness, there's a difference because he is here a party to the lawsuit and not just merely witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: What does this procedural difference consist of when you hear someone in the capacity of a party to the proceedings or if you hear him as a witness?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJOVIC
utterances.text: Well, this does not happen that often.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: Very well, General. Let me rephrase.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, I was merely waiting for the interpretation to catch up.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: I apologise. Go ahead with your answer.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJOVIC
utterances.text: This happens only seldomly when the case that is made for a lawsuit is not backed sufficiently, it can be additionally supported by the evidence of -- given by the plaintiff where he would give his -- put his case orally, give his submissions, and clarify matters. Since he is not being heard as a witness, he is not under the obligation to tell the truth in presenting his case under the law. He may even stay silent on some matters, and this is typical of this situation where the plaintiff filing a lawsuit withheld certain information, but the situation was accepted as such and a judgement rendered. So the prosecutor was heard here as a party trying to shed light on certain matters and not as a witness. The prosecutor, or rather, the plaintiff.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: General, tell us what sort of consequences would befall a witness giving false testimony before a court of law?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJOVIC
utterances.text: When a witness is heard in whatever the proceedings, be it a lawsuit or criminal proceedings, if he gives false testimony, he may be prosecuted for that. However, if we compare this with the hearing of a plaintiff as a party to proceedings and if we compare that with the witness being heard in criminal proceedings, especially in light of the legislation in Serbia today, he need not speak on matters which may incriminate him, or which may expose him to shame, disgrace, or even great material damage. Even in such circumstances, the witness need not give full testimony, whereas in all the other circumstances, he has to give full testimony and tell the truth. So that's the basic difference between a witness being heard and a party to the proceedings being heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: Thank you, General. We are now going to move to another topic. Can you please look at the next document in your binder?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And in e-court, can I kindly have 65 ter document 01147D. That's a Defence document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: General, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, although this is a poor photocopy, but I do recognise it. This is a document issued by the military court in Belgrade. The trial chamber issued this ruling. I presided over this chamber as the president of the court. This is a rejection of the request by the ICTY to hand over Milan Mrksic with Sljivancanin and Miroslav Radic to the Court in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, for the counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Microphone, Mr. Zorko.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour, once again.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: General, could you look at page 2, I'm going to ask you for the reasons for you delivering such a ruling. Paragraph 1 on page 2 in B/C/S and should be the same page in English as well. Yes, that's right. So look at paragraph 1 on this page. Can you please comment on it?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJOVIC
utterances.text: Of course. When the trial chamber deliberated on this request, it conducted a certain procedure, and in the course of that procedure the essential thing was to establish the number of facts, that is whether those were citizens of the FRY. Since we established that all the three persons were indeed citizens of the FRY, according to Article 17, para 3 of the constitution, does not allow extradition of citizens of the FRY to another state, and the same is provided by the Law on Criminal Procedure which stipulates that a request by any foreign court can be complied with only in case of foreign citizens and not the citizens of the state that received the request. So based on these provisions, the chamber rejected the ICTY's request for extradition of the three above-named individuals. This ruling was sent ex officio to the supreme military court for reconsideration and the supreme military court confirmed the ruling, and subsequently it was acted in accordance with the constitution of the then FRY.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I thought you were going to ask a question. If not -- thank you. I'd like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D429. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: General, can you please look at document 01148D, 65 ter Defence document. Can you please just tell us -- but let's wait a minute for the document to appear on the screens. General, is this the decision of the supreme military court that you just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's the decision of the supreme military court confirming the ruling of the military court in Belgrade which rendered this ruling final at this stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would also like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D430. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: General, can you please look at the next document in your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And in e-court, can we please have document 01313D.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: General, what is this document about?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJOVIC
utterances.text: This is the Law on Co-operation of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia with the International Tribunal for the Prosecution of Persons Responsible for Serious Violations of International Humanitarian Law Committed Since 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: Can you tell us the date of this "Official Gazette," when this law was published?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJOVIC
utterances.text: This law was adopted in April 2000. I can't see the date here and it was published in the "Official Gazette" on the 11th of April, 2002. It was adopted by the federal Assembly and this law regulates co-operation and it provides for a legal possibility for extradition of perpetrators of serious violation of International Humanitarian Law committed in the territory of the former Yugoslavia. Pursuant to this law there was legal basis sufficient for extradition of the perpetrators as requested by this Tribunal, and it was acted upon accordingly. Before that is there was no legal possibility to effect this. No court was allowed to break the law in such a way.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: General, can we please just confirming according to line 18 it says that the law was adopted in April 2000?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJOVIC
utterances.text: No, in April 2002.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document into evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D431. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: General, can you please look at the next document in your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And in e-court can we please have 01314D?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: General, I would just like to hear a brief comment of yours on this next document. Could you just please wait for the document to appear on the screens. Can you tell us briefly what the document is about?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJOVIC
utterances.text: Here we see the law on the amendment to the Law on Co-operation of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia with the ICTY, et cetera. The point of this law was that in the meantime, the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and its order were re-organised and subsequently became a state community of Serbia and Montenegro. Based on that, certain terminology and certain terms had to be changed and certain organs such as council of ministers, et cetera, had to be remained. So only these changes and amendments were effected in the language of the actually previous law. There were no other substantial changes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: Thank you, General. We are now going to move to a different subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have in e-court Prosecution Exhibit number -- I am sorry, before that I would like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D432. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Can we please have on e-court document P1747. I believe that we have the wrong translation, that it does not correspond to the original. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: So, General, we see what kind of document this is. Can you please tell us what can you see from this document?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJOVIC
utterances.text: This is a diploma issued by the national defence school in Belgrade, which is an integral part of the Yugoslav Army. It is in the name of Vinko Pandurevic. And further on it says that he finished -- or rather, attended the national defence school in 1997 and 1998, that his grade was 9.40, which is excellent, and we see in the bottom, the signature and the stamp of the national defence school. The diploma was issued on the 28th of January, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Can we please now have in e-court P2093. And we can remove the current document from our screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: And I would kindly ask you, General, to look at the next document that you have in your binder. Can you tell us, please, what kind of document can with see here?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJOVIC
utterances.text: This is a bill of indictment issued by the military disciplinary prosecutor to the military disciplinary court of the General Staff of the Yugoslav Army against Vinko Pandurevic for a specific disciplinary violation pursuant to the Law on the Yugoslav Army and the violation was that in the course of resolving his housing problems in Belgrade and while submitting an application to be given a flat with an indefinite term of lease, did not mention, or failed to mention the fact that previously he had been given a flat in Mali Zvornik and that he had actually bought this flat and later on sold it. This disqualifies him as someone who is entitled to apply for a new flat because on the 5th of May, 1998, he concluded a contract which is a period while he was attending the school of national defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: Thank you, General. From this document, can you tell us when this violation was committed and on the basis of what are you drawing such a conclusion?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJOVIC
utterances.text: According to the statement of reasons in this below entitlement the violation was committed on the date on which he concluded the contract on the lease of the flat, because at that time he failed to mention the fact that he already had a flat assigned to him on the 5th of May, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Can you tell us who this offence was committed against or to whose disadvantage was this offence committed?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJOVIC
utterances.text: The flat was assigned by the flat administration for housing of the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia on the basis of the request and attending documentation, so the injured party and the consequences of this disciplinary offence was the housing administration or the person whose flat this was to lease out, which is the Army of Yugoslavia. And this was a serious offence of military discipline which stipulated that all provisions and norms governing military service must be abided by.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: Now, we see that this bill of indictment was sent by the competent authority, which is in this case the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia. I apologise, it's the military disciplinary court and prosecutor. What I want to ask you specifically is this: Who had the authority to launch these disciplinary proceedings and what gave that person the authority to do so?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR GOJOVIC
utterances.text: Well, we have to go back to the previous piece of information in order to clarify that and look at the diploma that was issued to Pandurevic because from that diploma we can see that he attended the school of national defence and had completed that course. And that was attached to the General Staff. The school is within the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia and as a student there he committed this disciplinary offence. So in order to launch an investigation and initiate these proceedings, it was the chief of the national defence school whose job it was to launch the investigation and that the officer who was superior in the national defence school to make the decision to place it under the authority of the military disciplinary court. So that came before this bill of indictment which was compiled on the basis of the previous proposals. So during the time he committed the offence, he was attending the school. Those who attending the national defence school, regardless of which unit they came from, it was the chief of the school who was in charge and who had the authority to take disciplinary measures and proceedings in the Army of Yugoslavia, and that was true for all the people attending the military schools and their courses regardless of which unit or army they came from. So that's what I can say linked to the school and the service.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZORKO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Thank you, General. I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zorko. Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Your Honours, thank you. Yes, I will have some cross-examination but I wonder if we can adjourn early today and reconvene tomorrow. I think I can significantly shorten my proposed cross-examination of General Gojovic, and I understand that he is the only witness listed for this week.
